IF YES TO EITHER: How different is this from the way you were before (TRAUMATIC EVENT)? IF LIFETIME RATING OF "+": Has this also happened in the past month, since (ONE MONTH AGO)? How often? Past month rated separately.

questions.interviewer_text: ...have you done reckless things, like driving dangerously, or drinking or using drugs without caring about the consequences?
questions.criterion_description: 2. Reckless or self-destructive behavior.
questions.notes: IF NO: How about hurting yourself on purpose or trying to kill yourself? (What did you do?) IF YES TO EITHER: How different is this from the way you were before (TRAUMATIC EVENT)? IF LIFETIME RATING OF "+": Has this also happened in the past month? How often? Past month rated separately.

questions.interviewer_text: ...have you noticed that you have been more watchful or on guard? (What are some examples?)
questions.criterion_description: 3. Hypervigilance.
questions.notes: IF NO: Have you been extra aware of your surroundings and your environment? IF LIFETIME RATING OF "+": Has this also happened in the past month? How often? Past month rated separately.

questions.interviewer_text: ...have you been jumpy or easily startled, like by sudden noises? (Is this a change from before [TRAUMATIC EVENT]?)
questions.criterion_description: 4. Exaggerated startle response.
questions.notes: IF LIFETIME RATING OF "+": Has this also happened in the past month? How often? Past month rated separately.

questions.interviewer_text: ...have you had trouble concentrating? (What are some examples? (Is this a change from before [TRAUMATIC EVENT]?)
questions.criterion_description: 5. Problems with concentration.
questions.notes: IF LIFETIME RATING OF "+": Has this also happened in the past month? How often? Past month rated separately.

questions.interviewer_text: Since (TRAUMATIC EVENT)... ...how have you been sleeping since (TRAUMATIC EVENT)? (Is this a change from before [TRAUMATIC EVENT]?) IF LIFETIME RATING OF "+": Has this also happened in the past month? How often?
questions.criterion_description: 6. Sleep disturbance (e.g., difficulty falling or staying asleep or restless sleep).
questions.notes: Past month also rated: − or +

questions.criterion_description: AT LEAST TWO OF THE ABOVE CRITERION E SXS (G31–G36) ARE RATED "+". If other reported traumatic events, consider returning to G13 and reassessing PTSD for that event. Otherwise, go to H1 (ADHD), page 86.
questions.notes: Criterion E met past month also rated: NO or YES

questions.interviewer_text: About how long did these (PTSD SXS RATED "+") last altogether?
questions.criterion_description: F. Duration of the disturbance [symptoms in Criteria B (G19), C (G22), D (G30), and E (G37)] is more than 1 month. If other reported traumatic events, consider returning to G13 and reassessing PTSD for that event. Otherwise, go to H1 (ADHD), page 86.

questions.interviewer_text: IF UNCLEAR: What effect did (PTSD SXS) have on your life? ASK THE FOLLOWING QUESTIONS ONLY AS NEEDED: How have (PTSD SXS) affected your relationships or your interactions with other people? (Have [PTSD SXS] caused you any problems in your relationships with your family, romantic partner, or friends?) How have (PTSD SXS) affected your work/school? (How about your attendance at work/school? Have [PTSD SXS] made it more difficult to do your work/schoolwork? Have [PTSD SXS] affected the quality of your work/schoolwork?) How have [PTSD SXS] affected your ability to take care of things at home? What about being involved in things that are important to you, like religious activities, physical exercise, or hobbies? Have (PTSD SXS) affected any other important part of your life? IF HAVE NOT INTERFERED WITH LIFE: How much have you been bothered or upset by (PTSD SXS)? IF LIFETIME RATING OF "+": How have (PTSD SXS) affected your life in the past month?
questions.criterion_description: G. The disturbance causes clinically significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning. If other reported traumatic events, consider returning to G13 and reassessing PTSD for that event. Otherwise, go to H1 (ADHD), page 86.
questions.notes: Past month also rated: − or +

questions.interviewer_text: Have you been drinking a lot or using a lot of drugs since (TRAUMATIC EVENT)? Tell me about that. How much have you been (drinking/using [DRUGS])? (Do you think your problems since [TRAUMATIC EVENT] are more due to your [drinking/(DRUG) use] rather than to your reaction to [TRAUMATIC EVENT] itself?)
questions.criterion_description: H. The disturbance is not attributable to the physiological effects of a substance (e.g., medication, alcohol) or another medical condition.
questions.notes: If other reported traumatic events, consider returning to G13 and reassessing PTSD for that event. Otherwise, go to H1 (ADHD), next page.

questions.criterion_description: CRITERIA B (G19), C (G22), D (G30), and E (G37) ARE RATED "YES" FOR PAST MONTH AND CRITERION G (G39) (CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE) IS RATED "+" FOR PAST MONTH.
questions.notes: If YES: Past Hx and/or Current. Diagnose: Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (current). Continue with H1 (ADHD), next page.

questions.interviewer_text: Over the past several years, have you been easily distracted or disorganized? IF NO: Over the past several years, have you had a lot of difficulty sitting still or waiting your turn?
questions.criterion_description: A. A persistent pattern of inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity that interferes with functioning or development, as characterized by (1) and/or (2):
questions.notes: IF THERE IS NO EVIDENCE THAT THE PERSON HAS BEEN DISTRACTED, DISORGANIZED, IMPULSIVE, OR UNABLE TO SIT STILL OVER THE PAST 6 MONTHS, CHECK HERE ___ AND GO TO I1 (Screening), page 91.

questions.criterion_label: Inattention criterion a - Attention to details
questions.interviewer_text: ...have you often missed important details or made mistakes at work (or school) or while taking care of things at home? Please give me some examples. (Have you often made mistakes balancing your checkbook or paying bills? Have other people complained that you don't pay enough attention to detail or that your work is careless?)
questions.criterion_description: a. Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes in schoolwork, at work, or during other activities (e.g., overlooks or misses details, work is inaccurate).

questions.interviewer_text: ...have you often had trouble staying focused on things like reading a book, following a conversation, or doing household chores? Give me some examples.
questions.criterion_description: b. Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities (e.g., has difficulty remaining focused during lectures, conversations, or lengthy reading).

questions.interviewer_text: ...has anyone commented or complained that you haven't seemed to be listening or that your mind was elsewhere while they were talking? Tell me about that. (How often has this happened?) (Has this happened even when nothing else is going on...when there are no obvious distractions?)
questions.criterion_description: c. Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly (e.g., mind seems elsewhere, even in the absence of any obvious distraction).

questions.interviewer_text: ...have you often started things and then dropped them without finishing because you lost your focus or got sidetracked? Give me some examples.
questions.criterion_description: d. Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace (e.g., starts tasks but quickly loses focus and is easily sidetracked).

questions.interviewer_text: In the past 6 months, since (SIX MONTHS AGO)... ...have you had trouble organizing things at home or at work, or staying on top of things? Tell me about that. (Are your desk and closet so messy and disorganized that you have had trouble finding things? Have you had trouble managing your time so that you have been late a lot or missed appointments or failed to meet deadlines?)
questions.criterion_description: e. Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities (e.g., difficulty managing sequential tasks; difficulty keeping materials and belongings in order; messy, disorganized work; has poor time management; fails to meet deadlines).

questions.criterion_label: Inattention criterion f: Avoids sustained mental effort
questions.interviewer_text: ...have you typically avoided or strongly disliked tasks or jobs that require concentrating on details for extended periods, things like preparing a report for work or writing a paper? Give me some examples of the types of tasks or jobs you have avoided or disliked.
questions.criterion_description: f. Often avoids, dislikes, or is reluctant to engage in tasks that require sustained mental effort (e.g., schoolwork or homework, for older adolescents and adults, preparing reports, completing forms, reviewing lengthy papers).

questions.interviewer_text: ...have you often lost or misplaced things like your wallet, your glasses, your keys, or your cell phone? How about files at work or tools you needed for work? Tell me about that.
questions.criterion_description: g. Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities (e.g., school materials, pencils, books, tools, wallets, keys, paperwork, eyeglasses, mobile telephones).

questions.interviewer_text: ...have you been very easily distracted by things going on around you that most others would have easily ignored, like a car honking or other people talking? Tell me about that. IF NO: Have you often gotten distracted by your own thoughts that were unrelated to what you were doing?
questions.criterion_description: h. Is often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).

questions.criterion_label: Inattention criterion i: Forgetful in daily activities
questions.interviewer_text: ...have you often been very forgetful, for example, forgetting to return phone calls, forgetting to pay bills, or forgetting appointments? Tell me about that.
questions.criterion_description: i. Is often forgetful in everyday activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
AT LEAST FIVE OF THE ABOVE CRITERION A1 (INATTENTION) SXS (H2–H10) ARE RATED "+".
questions.notes: ADHD Criterion A1 is met.

questions.interviewer_text: ...have you often fidgeted or squirmed or tapped your foot when you were in a situation where you have had to sit still, like on a plane, in class, or at meetings? Tell me about that.
questions.criterion_description: a. Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.

questions.interviewer_text: ...have you often left your seat when you were expected to stay seated, for example, during a religious service, in a movie theater, in class, or at meetings? Tell me about that.
questions.criterion_description: b. Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected (e.g., leaves his or her place in the classroom, in the office or other workplace, or in other situations that require remaining in place).

questions.criterion_label: Runs about or climbs inappropriately / feels restless
questions.interviewer_text: ...have you often felt physically restless, especially when you had to stay put for a while? Tell me about that.
questions.criterion_description: c. Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)

questions.criterion_label: Unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly
questions.interviewer_text: ...have you often been unable to do something quietly in your spare time, like reading a book? Tell me about that. (Have others said that you talk too much or that you make too much noise when you are supposed to be quiet?)
questions.criterion_description: d. Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.

questions.criterion_label: "On the go" or "driven by a motor"
questions.interviewer_text: ...have you often felt like you always have to be moving or doing something? Have you been uncomfortable being still for any length of time? Have others told you that you are hard to keep up with? Have other people told you that being with you is exhausting or draining? Tell me about that.
questions.criterion_description: e. Is often "on the go," acting as if "driven by a motor" (e.g., is unable to be or uncomfortable being still for extended time, as in restaurants, meetings; may be experienced by others as being restless or difficult to keep up with).

questions.interviewer_text: ...have you often talked too much? Tell me about that. (Have other people complained that you talk too much? How often does this happen?)
questions.criterion_description: f. Often talks excessively.

questions.interviewer_text: ...have you often finished people's sentences or blurted out an answer before the other person finished asking the question? Tell me about that. (Has it often been hard for you to wait your turn in conversations?)
questions.criterion_description: g. Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed (e.g., completes people's sentences; cannot wait for turn in conversation.

questions.interviewer_text: ...have you often had trouble waiting for your "turn," like while waiting in line or ordering at a restaurant? Describe what happens.
questions.criterion_description: h. Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn (e.g., while waiting in line).

questions.criterion_label: Hyperactivity-Impulsivity Criterion A2 - Often interrupts or intrudes
questions.interviewer_text: In the past 6 months, since (SIX MONTHS AGO)... ...have you often interrupted other people while they were talking or barged into others' conversations? What about jumping in to take over what someone else was doing, like when someone was taking too long to unlock a door or fix something? Give me some examples of when that has happened.
questions.criterion_description: i. Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities; may start using other people's things without asking or receiving permission; for adolescents and adults, may intrude into or take over what others are doing).
AT LEAST FIVE OF THE ABOVE CRITERION A2 (HYPERACTIVITY-IMPULSIVITY) SXS (H12–H20) ARE RATED "+".
questions.notes: ADHD Criterion A2 is met.

questions.criterion_label: Combined Criterion A1 or A2 check
questions.criterion_description: AT LEAST FIVE SXS IN CRITERION A1 (H11) OR CRITERION A2 (H21) ARE RATED "+".

questions.criterion_label: Criterion B - Age of onset before 12
questions.interviewer_text: How old were you when you started having some of these (SXS RATED "+")? (Was this before you were 12?) Tell me about that. (Did teachers complain that you were not paying attention or that you talked too much in class? Were you ever sent to the principal's office because of your behavior? Did your parents complain that you were not able to sit still, that you were very messy, or that you were never ready on time?)
questions.criterion_description: B. Several inattentive or hyperactive-impulsive symptoms were present prior to age 12 years.

questions.interviewer_text: IF UNKNOWN: These things you've told me about, like (SXS RATED "+"), have they happened in more than one area of your life, like at work and at home? Or are they confined to just one situation, for example, only at work but never when you are with friends or family?
questions.criterion_description: C. Several inattentive or hyperactive-impulsive symptoms are present in two or more settings (e.g., at home, school, or work; with friends or relatives; in other activities).

questions.interviewer_text:
IF UNCLEAR: What effect have (ADHD SXS) had on your life in the past 6 months, since (6 MONTHS AGO)?

ASK THE FOLLOWING QUESTIONS ONLY AS NEEDED:

How have (ADHD SXS) affected your relationships or your interactions with other people? (Have [ADHD SXS] caused you any problems in your relationships with your family, romantic partner, or friends?)

How have (ADHD SXS) affected your work/school? (How about your attendance at work/school? Have [ADHD SXS] made it more difficult to do your work/schoolwork? Have [ADHD SXS] affected the quality of your work/schoolwork?)

How have (ADHD SXS) affected your ability to take care of things at home? Have your (ADHD SXS) made it hard for you to do things that are important to you, like religious activities, physical exercise, sports, or hobbies?

Have (ADHD SXS) affected any other important part of your life?
questions.criterion_description: D. There is clear evidence that the symptoms interfere with, or reduce the quality of, social, academic, or occupational functioning.

questions.criterion_label: Symptoms not better explained by psychotic disorder
questions.interviewer_text: IF A PSYCHOTIC DISORDER HAS BEEN DIAGNOSED: Did you have (ADHD SXS RATED "+") before you had (SXS OF PSYCHOTIC DISORDER)?
questions.criterion_description: E. The symptoms do not occur exclusively during the course of Schizophrenia or another Psychotic Disorder and are not better explained by another mental disorder (e.g., Depressive Disorder, Bipolar Disorder, Anxiety Disorder, Dissociative Disorder, Personality Disorder, Substance Intoxication or Withdrawal).
questions.notes:
Diagnose: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (current)
Combined Presentation: If Criterion A1/item H11, page 87 (inattention) and Criterion A2/item H21, page 89 (hyperactivity-impulsivity) are met for the past 6 months.
Predominantly Inattentive Presentation: If Criterion A1/item H11, page 87 (inattention) is met but Criterion A2/item H21, page 89 (hyperactivity-impulsivity) is not met for the past 6 months.
Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation: If Criterion A2/item H21, page 89 (hyperactivity-impulsivity) is met but Criterion A1/item H11, page 87 (inattention) is not met for the past 6 months.

questions.interviewer_text: Looking back over your menstrual cycles for the past 12 months, since (ONE YEAR AGO), have you had mood symptoms such as anger, irritability, anxiety, or depression that developed before your period and then went away during the week after your period?
questions.criterion_description: IF YES: After your period began, did the problems disappear for at least a week? IF YES TO BOTH: Consider Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder (DSM-5, p. 171; User's Guide, p. 116).
questions.notes: IF PATIENT IS A BIOLOGICAL MALE, POSTMENOPAUSAL FEMALE, PREGNANT FEMALE, OR FEMALE WITH HYSTERECTOMY PLUS OOPHORECTOMY, SKIP TO THE NEXT QUESTION (I2). If YES, possible Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder.

questions.interviewer_text: In the past 6 months, since (6 MONTHS AGO), have there been things that have made you especially anxious or afraid, like flying, seeing blood, getting a shot, heights, closed places, or certain kinds of animals or insects?
questions.criterion_description: IF YES: Consider Specific Phobia (DSM-5, p. 197; User's Guide, p. 117).
questions.notes: If YES, possible Specific Phobia.

questions.interviewer_text: In the past 6 months, have you been especially anxious about being separated from people you're attached to (like your parents, children, or partner)?
questions.criterion_description: IF YES: Consider Separation Anxiety Disorder (DSM-5, p. 190; User's Guide, p. 118).
questions.notes: If YES, possible Separation Anxiety Disorder.

questions.interviewer_text: In the past month, since (ONE MONTH AGO), have you found it difficult to throw out, sell, or give away things?
questions.criterion_description: IF YES: Consider Hoarding Disorder (DSM-5, p. 247; User's Guide, p. 119).
questions.notes: If YES, possible Hoarding Disorder.

questions.interviewer_text: In the past month, have you been very concerned that there is something wrong with your physical appearance or the way one or more parts of your body look?
questions.criterion_description: IF YES: Consider Body Dysmorphic Disorder (DSM-5, p. 242; User's Guide, p. 119).
questions.notes: If YES, possible Body Dysmorphic Disorder.

questions.interviewer_text: In the past month, have you been repeatedly pulling out hair from anywhere on your body other than for cosmetic reasons?
questions.criterion_description: IF YES: Consider Trichotillomania (Hair-Pulling Disorder) (DSM-5, p. 251; User's Guide, p. 120).
questions.notes: If YES, possible Trichotillomania.

questions.interviewer_text: In the past month, have you been repeatedly picking at your skin with your fingernails, tweezers, pins, or other objects?
questions.criterion_description: IF YES: Consider Excoriation (Skin-Picking) Disorder (DSM-5, p. 254; User's Guide, p. 120).
questions.notes: POSSIBLE EXCORIATION DISORDER

questions.interviewer_text: Over the past 3 months, since (3 MONTHS AGO), has a major concern of yours been that you are not getting enough good sleep or not feeling rested?
questions.criterion_description: IF YES: Consider Insomnia Disorder (DSM-5, p. 362; User's Guide, p. 121).
questions.notes: POSSIBLE INSOMNIA DISORDER

questions.interviewer_text: Over the past 3 months, have you often had days when you were sleepy despite having slept for at least 7 hours?
questions.criterion_description: IF YES: Consider Hypersomnolence Disorder (DSM-5, p. 368; User's Guide, p. 121).
questions.notes: POSSIBLE HYPERSOMNOLENCE DISORDER

questions.interviewer_text: In the past 3 months, have you had a time when you weighed much less than other people thought you ought to weigh?
questions.criterion_description: IF YES: Consider Anorexia Nervosa (DSM-5, p. 338; User's Guide, p. 122).
questions.notes: POSSIBLE ANOREXIA NERVOSA

questions.interviewer_text: In the past 3 months, have you had eating binges, that is, times when you couldn't resist eating a lot of food or stop eating once you started?
questions.criterion_description: IF YES: Consider Bulimia Nervosa (DSM-5, p. 345; User's Guide, p. 122) or Binge-Eating Disorder (DSM-5, p. 350; User's Guide, p. 123).
questions.notes: POSSIBLE BULIMIA NERVOSA OR BINGE-EATING DISORDER

questions.interviewer_text: In the past month, since (ONE MONTH AGO), have you been uninterested in food in general or have you kept forgetting to eat?
questions.criterion_description: IF NO: In the past month, have you avoided eating a lot of foods because of the way they look or the way they feel in your mouth? IF NO: In the past month, have you avoided eating a lot of different foods because you are afraid you won't be able to swallow or that you will choke, gag, or throw up? IF YES TO ANY: Consider Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder (DSM-5, p. 334; User's Guide, p. 123).
questions.notes: POSSIBLE AVOIDANT/RESTRICTIVE FOOD INTAKE DISORDER

questions.interviewer_text: Over the past 6 months, since (6 MONTHS AGO), have you been bothered by any physical symptoms?
questions.criterion_description: IF YES: Consider Somatic Symptom Disorder (DSM-5, p. 311; User's Guide, p. 124).
questions.notes: POSSIBLE SOMATIC SYMPTOM DISORDER

questions.interviewer_text: Over the past 6 months, have you spent a lot of time thinking that you have, or will get, a serious disease?
questions.criterion_description: IF YES: Consider Illness Anxiety Disorder (DSM-5, p. 315; User's Guide, p. 124).
questions.notes: If YES, possible ILLNESS ANXIETY DISORDER

questions.interviewer_text: In the past 12 months, since (ONE YEAR AGO), have you had periods in which you frequently lost control of your temper and ended up yelling or getting into arguments with others?
questions.criterion_description: IF YES TO EITHER: Consider Intermittent Explosive Disorder (DSM-5, p. 466; User's Guide, p. 125).
questions.notes: IF NO: In the past year, have you lost your temper so that you shoved, hit, kicked, or threw something at a person or an animal or damaged someone's property? If YES to either, possible INTERMITTENT EXPLOSIVE DISORDER

questions.interviewer_text: In the past 12 months, have you regularly gambled or regularly bought lottery tickets?
questions.criterion_description: IF YES: Consider Gambling Disorder (DSM-5, p. 585; User's Guide, p. 126).
questions.notes: If YES, possible GAMBLING DISORDER. After this, Go to J1, (Adjustment Disorder), next page.

questions.criterion_label: Criterion A - Identifiable stressor and temporal relationship
questions.interviewer_text: IF UNKNOWN: Did anything happen to you before (SXS) began? IF YES: Tell me about what happened. Do you think that (STRESSOR) had anything to do with your developing (SXS)? IF SINGLE EVENT: How long after (STRESSOR) did you first develop (SXS)? (Was it within 3 months?) IF CHRONIC STRESSOR: How long after (STRESSOR) began did you first develop (SXS)? (Was it within 3 months?)
questions.criterion_description: A. The development of emotional or behavioral symptoms in response to an identifiable stressor(s) occurring within 3 months of the onset of the stressor(s).
questions.notes: INFORMATION OBTAINED FROM OVERVIEW OF PRESENT ILLNESS WILL USUALLY BE SUFFICIENT TO RATE THIS CRITERION. CONSIDER ADJUSTMENT DISORDER ONLY IF 1) THERE IS AN IDENTIFIED STRESSOR AND 2) THERE ARE SYMPTOMS OCCURRING IN THE PAST 6 MONTHS THAT DO NOT MEET THE CRITERIA FOR ANOTHER DSM-5 DISORDER.

questions.interviewer_text: IF UNKNOWN: What effect did (SXS) have on your life? ASK THE FOLLOWING QUESTIONS AS NEEDED: How have (SXS) affected your relationships or your interactions with other people? (Have [SXS] caused you any problems in your relationships with your family, romantic partner, or friends?) How have (SXS) affected your work/school? (How about your attendance at work/school? Have [SXS] made it more difficult to do your work/schoolwork? Have [SXS] affected the quality of your work/schoolwork?) How have (SXS) affected your ability to take care of things at home? What about being involved in things that are important to you, like religious activities, physical exercise, or hobbies? Have (SXS) affected any other important part of your life? IF DO NOT INTERFERE WITH LIFE: How much have you been bothered or upset by having (SXS)?
questions.criterion_description: B. These symptoms or behaviors are clinically significant, as evidenced by one or both of the following: 1. Marked distress that is out of proportion to the severity or intensity of the stressor, taking into account the external context and the cultural factors that might influence symptom severity and presentation. 2. Significant impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning.

questions.criterion_label: Criterion C - Not another mental disorder
questions.interviewer_text:
(Have you had this kind of reaction many times before?)

(Were you having these [SXS] even before [STRESSOR] happened?)
questions.criterion_description: The stress-related disturbance does not meet the criteria for another mental disorder and is not merely an exacerbation of a preexisting mental disorder [including Personality Disorder].

questions.interviewer_text: IF UNKNOWN: Did someone close to you die just before (SXS)?
questions.criterion_description: D. The symptoms do not represent normal bereavement.

questions.criterion_label: Criterion E - Duration after stressor termination
questions.interviewer_text: IF UNKNOWN: How long has it been since (STRESSOR AND ITS CONSEQUENCES) was over?
questions.criterion_description: E. Once the stressor or its consequences have terminated, the symptoms do not persist for more than an additional 6 months.
questions.notes: Diagnose: Adjustment Disorder (current) with subtypes: With Depressed Mood, With Anxiety, With Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood, With Disturbance of Conduct, With Mixed Disturbance of Emotions and Conduct, Unspecified.
